subject: anatomy
title: Muscle and nervous tissue histology: sarcomere, myelin and neuroglia

steps.tx: Skeletal muscle fibres show **cross striations** because of the repeating **sarcomere**, the unit running from one Z line to the next. The **A band** is dark and contains the full length of thick myosin filaments. The **I band** is light, contains only thin actin filaments, and is bisected by the Z line. The **H zone**, in the middle of the A band, contains only myosin.
steps.say: Skeletal muscle fibres show cross striations because of the repeating sarcomere, the unit running from one Z line to the next. The A band is dark and contains the full length of thick myosin filaments. The I band is light, contains only thin actin filaments, and is bisected by the Z line. The H zone, in the middle of the A band, contains only myosin.

steps.tx: Actin is anchored to the Z line by **alpha actinin**, while myosin is held at the M line by **myomesin**. **Titin** acts as a spring and is absent in smooth muscle. Desmin is an intermediate filament of muscle cells and acts as a useful marker. Microfilaments are actin and myosin, which drive contraction.

vis.alt: Diagram of a sarcomere relaxed and contracted: thin actin filaments anchored to Z lines, thick myosin in the A band centred on the M line; on contraction the I band and H zone shorten while the A band stays the same length.
vis.caption: Contraction shortens the I band and H zone; the A band keeps its length.

steps.tx: Cardiac muscle forms a functional **syncytium** through **intercalated discs**, which sit at the Z line and contain gap junctions. Cardiac fibres branch and interdigitate, have one centrally placed nucleus, and show cross striations. Smooth muscle lacks sarcomeres and striations, and its cells are spindle shaped. Skeletal fibres have multiple peripheral nuclei.

steps.tx: Neuroglia support neurons. **Astrocytes** form the **blood-brain barrier** with endothelial cells and regulate potassium. **Microglia** are phagocytic and are of mesodermal origin, acting as CNS macrophages. **Ependymal cells** line the ventricles. Satellite cells support PNS neuron cell bodies. Nissl bodies, which are rough endoplasmic reticulum, make proteins in neurons.

steps.tx: Glia must be matched to the correct division of the nervous system. **Oligodendrocytes** wrap axons with myelin in the central nervous system, whereas **Schwann cells** perform this role for peripheral nerves. **Ependymal cells** form a simple epithelial lining over the ventricles and central canal, and their cilia help move cerebrospinal fluid. Keep these pairings straight, because examiners often test them directly.
steps.say: Let's match each glial cell to its correct location. Oligodendrocytes make myelin in the central nervous system, while Schwann cells make myelin for peripheral nerves. Ependymal cells line the ventricles and the central canal, and their cilia help circulate cerebrospinal fluid. Examiners often test these pairings, so link each cell to its territory as you revise.

vis.alt: Table matching glial cells to location and function: oligodendrocytes myelinate many CNS axons, Schwann cells myelinate one PNS segment, astrocytes form the blood brain barrier, microglia are the CNS macrophages from mesoderm, ependymal cells line the ventricles.
vis.caption: Oligodendrocyte: CNS myelin, many axons. Schwann cell: PNS myelin, one segment of one axon.
